spec.findings: (a) Response shapes match the request. GET /api/routes returns [{route_id, color, direction, name, stop_count}] (app/schemas.py RouteListItem; SPEC 6.4). color is the lowercase token (yellow, blue, purple, grey, red, darkyellow), not a display label. Detail returns {type: FeatureCollection, features: [...]}: feature 0 is a LineString (coordinates [lng, lat], properties route_id, color, direction); then one Point per route_stop row in seq order (properties name, seq; coordinates [lng, lat]). Points do NOT carry stop_id or color. Detail 404 is {"error":"route_not_found","message":...}; the request treats any failure the same (one banner), so the error shape does not matter to the front end. /api/routes returns [] (200) when route data is empty (SPEC 12). (b) SPEC fixes no hex values except as examples: "#FACC15 and #B8860B" for yellow and darkyellow (SPEC 7). The request's yellow and darkyellow match those. The other four (#0052B4, #6A1B9A, #757575, #D32F2F) are unconstrained by SPEC. No conflict. SPEC requires colors defined once in web/map.js: consistent with request item 3. (c) Conflict: tests/api/test_static.py::test_root_serves_placeholder_page asserts "Hello world" in GET / text. Replacing web/index.html will fail it unless the page keeps that text or the test is edited. Other tests in that file (health, docs, /api/routes not shadowed, unknown path error shape) are unaffected. Not decided here; see clarification 1. (d) SPEC has no statement on Leaflet vendoring, licence file, or attribution wording beyond NFR-4 ("The page and README credit '(c) OpenStreetMap contributors'") and "No build step" (SPEC 3). SPEC Layout lists web/ as index.html, map.js, style.css; vendored files are additions, not a conflict. Static serving from web/ at / already exists (StaticFiles html=True), so vendored files are reachable at /leaflet.js etc. with no backend change. NFR-4 also requires the README credit, which the request's "no docs edits" excludes (clarification 4).

clarifications.q: Existing test tests/api/test_static.py::test_root_serves_placeholder_page asserts "Hello world" in GET /. The new page will not contain it. Options: (A) update/replace that one assertion in the test (e.g. assert the response is HTML containing the map container id), or (B) keep a hidden/visible "Hello world" in index.html. Recommended default: A, a minimal edit of that single test, since B pollutes the real page to satisfy a placeholder check. The request says "no backend changes"; a test edit is not backend, but needs owner OK because the request says "exactly this and nothing else".

Circular routes (yellow_out, purple_out, grey_out) pass the same real place twice, so the detail response contains two Point features with the same name and different seq. Request item 6 says "shared stop drawn once per route". Should a stop appearing twice on one route be drawn as one dot (dedupe by name within the route) or as two dots at identical coordinates? Recommended default: dedupe by name within a route (one dot per distinct stop name per route). Note the Points have no stop_id, so name is the only key.

If /api/routes returns a color token not among the six (cannot happen with the fixed registry, but the front end gets no guarantee), what should be drawn? Recommended default: treat as a load failure is overkill; skip no routes and draw that route in a neutral fallback is a new decision, so default is: not handled (registry is fixed and validated by validate.py).

NFR-4 and CLAUDE.md require the README to credit "(c) OpenStreetMap contributors" and DECISIONS.md to have an entry per SPEC Section 3 tool (Leaflet is one); the request forbids docs edits. Recommended default: out of scope for T008, tracked as a later docs slice; this task adds attribution on the page only.

Attribution text: request says show "(c) OpenStreetMap contributors". Leaflet's built-in attribution control would normally render it with a copyright symbol and a link to openstreetmap.org/copyright. Recommended default: render the literal text "(c) OpenStreetMap contributors" via the tile layer attribution (plain, with link to https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright allowed), and keep Leaflet's own "Leaflet" prefix as is.

user_stories.story: As a rider, I open the page and see a map of Angeles City with all six jeepney routes drawn in distinct colors.
As a rider, I see a legend that tells me which color is which route.
As a rider, I can click a stop dot to see its name.
As a rider, if routes cannot load or none exist, I see a clear message over the map instead of a blank or partial map.
As a maintainer, the OSM credit is visible and no third-party service is called at runtime except OSM tiles.

acceptance_criteria.c: web/ contains index.html, map.js, style.css, and vendored Leaflet 1.9.4: leaflet.js, leaflet.css, marker images (in the path leaflet.css expects), and the Leaflet BSD-2 licence file. Pass: files exist; index.html references only local files for scripts/styles (no CDN or other third-party URL besides OSM tile requests made by Leaflet).
GET / returns the page; GET of each vendored file path linked from index.html returns 200 (can be checked by pytest/curl against the static mount).
No build step: page works by serving web/ as-is; no package.json build, no bundler files added.

Colors are defined exactly once, in map.js, as yellow #FACC15, blue #0052B4, purple #6A1B9A, grey #757575, red #D32F2F, darkyellow #B8860B; line styling, stop dots and legend swatches all read from that single definition (grep: each hex appears once in web/ excluding vendored Leaflet; style.css contains none of them).
On load the page requests GET /api/routes, then GET /api/routes/{route_id} for every route_id returned, issued in parallel (browser network panel shows 9 detail requests overlapping).

Each LineString is drawn with its color group's color; out and back of the same color have identical color and style. GeoJSON [lng, lat] is converted so lines land in Angeles City (about lat 15.1-15.2, lng 120.5-120.7), not off the coast of Somalia.

Each stop is a small dot in its route's color (or clearly styled dot), drawn once per route per clarification 2; clicking a dot shows its name; dots do nothing else (no selection, no plan call, no highlight state).
After successful load the map view is fitted to the bounds of all loaded lines.
A legend lists exactly six entries with labels Yellow, Blue, Purple, Grey, Red, Dark yellow, each with its swatch color.
OSM tiles are used and the text "(c) OpenStreetMap contributors" is visible on the page (NFR-4).

Failure: if /api/routes or any one detail request fails (network error or non-2xx), no route lines or stop dots are drawn and a banner over the map shows exactly: We couldn't load the jeepney routes. Check your connection and refresh the page.
Empty data: if /api/routes returns [], a banner over the map shows exactly: No route data is available. No detail requests are made and no lines are drawn.
On success, no banner is visible.

Index contains one empty, visible container (e.g. aside id="panel") with no children, no text, no scripts attached to it; laid out beside/over the map for desktop only; no media queries or responsive CSS.
No changes to app/, sql/, data/, tests other than as resolved in clarification 1, SPEC.md, README.md, or docs/.
Existing pytest suite passes (with the clarification 1 resolution applied); visual criteria 5-14 are verified by the owner in a browser, not pytest.

assumptions.a: Relative URLs (/api/...) are used since the page is served by the same FastAPI app at /.
Route display labels (Yellow ... Dark yellow) map from the color token in map.js; the route name field from /api/routes is not shown in this slice.
Legend and banner live in index.html/style.css/map.js, not backend.
Banner for failure replaces any partial drawing: draw only after all 9 details succeed.

edge_cases.e: One of nine detail requests fails: nothing drawn, failure banner.
/api/routes returns [] (SPEC 12 unseeded start): empty banner, no legend requirement change (legend may still show six entries; see risks).
Circular route with duplicate stop name (clarification 2).
Out and back overlap on the same road: both drawn; same style.
/api/routes returns 500 or non-JSON: treated as failure.
Tiles fail to load (offline): routes still draw; no banner required.

risks.risk: Existing test fails on "Hello world" unless resolved (clarification 1).
Leaflet default marker images path: leaflet.css expects images/ relative to itself; wrong placement yields 404s for icons (only matters if markers used; dots are circle markers).
Legend shown while empty-data banner is up is unspecified; request is silent. Default: legend still renders; not tested.
Fitting bounds on lines only; stops outside lines are ignored per request.

dependencies.d: Leaflet 1.9.4 (npm package or official release), BSD-2 licensed, vendored.
Existing GET /api/routes and GET /api/routes/{route_id}; StaticFiles mount of web/ at / in app/main.py.
OSM tile servers at runtime (browser only).

spec.self_critique: Every story maps to criteria (map/colors 4-6, legend 9, click 7, messages 11-13, attribution 10). Criteria 5-14 are not pytest-testable; they are owner browser checks per the request. Biggest open risk: clarification 1 (the test) and clarification 2 (circular duplicates), which change observable behavior.
